title: US private credit: fast growth and redemption limits (default rate reported, not confirmed)
event_started: 2026 (default rate at a record 6.0% in April 2026)
what_happened: US private credit has grown to about $1.5 trillion outstanding, up 13.8% in a year. The Federal Reserve reports that some funds kept redemption limits and net flows stayed negative. A Fitch default rate of 6.2% for October has been reported but not yet read at Fitch.
how_it_reaches_markets: Losses at business development companies, banks and insurers that lend to or hold private credit; redemption pressure on non-traded funds; tighter credit for mid-sized companies.

sourced_facts.text: Federal Reserve Financial Stability Report (November 2026): private credit outstanding $1,504 billion, up 13.8% from 2025:Q2 to 2026:Q2 (Table 1.1)
Same report: 'Redemption requests at certain business development companies trended lower, though funds maintained redemption limits and net flows remained negative.'

Federal Reserve staff note, 2026-11-09: US private credit vehicles held about $1.9 trillion in assets at the end of 2025; BDCs 'tend to be more highly levered with an average debt-to-equity ratio around 1'

resolved_when_all: Fitch trailing-12-month private credit default rate below 4.0% for three consecutive monthly readings
Credit stress component of this ledger is Moderate or lower throughout the same period
worsened_when_any: A large private credit fund suspends or limits redemptions, or a bank discloses a private-credit-related loss above 1 billion dollars
Credit stress component of this ledger reaches High

relief_headlines_that_do_not_resolve_it: Record fundraising by private credit managers (new money raised says nothing about existing loans)
A one-month dip in the default rate (6.3% to 6.2% from September to October 2026)

superseded_sources.reason: Source rule of 2026-11-26: at least one primary source per card; commentary, blogs and reposts are not used as support
facts_as_first_written: Fitch: 6.2% trailing-12-month default rate to October 2026, 6.3% in September; 90 unique defaulters; 10.7% for issuers under 25 million dollars EBITDA versus 2.4% above 100 million (Max's Digest, 2026-11-18)
JPMorgan forecasts leveraged-loan defaults of 4.5% in 2027 and 4.75% in 2028 (Max's Digest)
Moody's: banks had extended nearly 300 billion dollars to private credit funds, BDCs and CLOs as of October 2025 (Forbes, 2026-05-24)
No fund redemption gate in November 2026 is stated in these sources
superseded_sources.summary_as_first_written: The Fitch trailing-12-month US private credit default rate stood at 6.2% in October 2026. Most default events are payment deferrals and maturity extensions rather than bankruptcies, and smaller borrowers default far more often. Banks and life insurers have large exposures to private credit funds.

counter_view.note: The strongest reason this card's reading may be wrong. AFMX's own judgment, using the facts listed on the card.
counter_view.text: Stress has not shown up in traded credit: the high-yield spread in this record is at 1 of 3 steps. The Federal Reserve reports that redemption requests have trended lower. The defaults may stay among small borrowers and never reach banks or public markets.

forecasts.basis: The default rate is reported at 6.2% and would have to be under 4.0% for three months. One fund of $1 billion or more newly limiting redemptions is enough to worsen the card, and limits already exist at some funds.
